the interaction of the C-F bond with a proximate π-orbital of a C═ C bond is a strong, non-covalent interaction that can be characterized by spectroscopic and theoretical methods.
we have synthesized two molecules in which a fluorinated group interacts in a proximate fashion with a C=C or a C-H bond.

we have synthesized two molecules, in each case containing a C-F bond that is proximately interacting with a π-system of a proximate C═C bond, and that we have also synthesized two other molecules, each of which has a C-F bond proximately interacting in a "head-on" fashion with a C-H bond of a proximate alkyl substituent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and study of molecules that contain unusual C-F bond interactions with proximate C-H bonds and C═C π-orbitals.
the synthesis and characterization of molecules that exhibit a C-F bond interacting with the π-systems of C=C bonds and with proximate C-H bonds.
the interaction of a fluorine atom with the π-systems of a C═O and a C═C double bond and also the interaction of a C-F and a proximate C- H bond.

these molecules are the first examples of a new class of compounds, in which a C-F bond is proximate to the π-system of an olefinic bond or to the σ-orbitals of an adjacent C-H bond.

the interaction of a C-F group proximately with the π-orbitaals of a proximate C═C bond is weak and is characterized by an elongation of both the F-C and C-C bonds and by a red shift of the C-C stretching vibration.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated the feasibility of synthesizing molecules in which the C-F bond is proximate to the π-system of an aromatic ring or proximate to a C-H bond, and that the spectroscopic characteristics of the resulting interactions are readily observed and interpreted.
a proximal fluorine atom can interact strongly with the π-orbita of a C=C bond, and that a C-F bond can also interact strongly with a proximate hydrogen atom.

the C-F bond is a very strong electron-withdrawing substituent, which is able to interact with proximate C-H bonds in a "head-on" manner and also with the π-systems of proximate C=C bonds in an "edge on" fashion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a fluorine atom positioned above a proximate C=C bond can interact with the π-orbitlals of that C=C bond, and that this interaction can be characterized by the spectroscopy of the proximate C-F bond.
the spectroscopic characteristics of the proximate C-F/C-C and C-F/H-C interactions are similar to those observed for the more familiar proximate C-H/C-C and C-H/H-C interactions.
